name: base-blocked-unlock-pickup
task: Pick up the blocking ball and the key, in either order, unlock the door, and then pick up the box in the other room.

value.feedback: CHANGES REQUIRED: the hard Existence(blocker_moved), Existence(has_door_key), and Existence(door_open) are redundant. Existence(target_picked_up) together with Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) already forces door_open; door_open with Precedence(blocker_moved, door_open) forces blocker_moved; door_open with Precedence(has_door_key, door_open) forces has_door_key. The task does command all four events, and 'Every way to finish includes' confirms all four are required, but the three Existence clauses only repeat what the chain forces and give them reward as goals of their own. Remove the three redundant Existence clauses and keep Existence(target_picked_up) with the three hard Precedence clauses (blocker_moved, door_open), (has_door_key, door_open), (door_open, target_picked_up).

NO CHANGES NEEDED: Existence(target_picked_up) with Precedence(door_open, target_picked_up) forces door_open, and the Precedences of blocker_moved and has_door_key to door_open force both events, matching 'pick up the ball and the key, in either order, unlock the door, then pick up the box'. The lack of any order between blocker_moved and has_door_key correctly reflects 'in either order', and every way to finish includes all four events.
